root_cause_label: Knowledge Gap: Agent cannot conceive how to express chess move generation as regex substitution patterns
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent correctly identified the legal moves for the example position but lacked the algorithmic insight to construct general regex-replacement pairs, then got trapped in a repeated str_replace tool failure loop and ultimately abandoned the task as infeasible.
t_err_evidence: At step 14 the agent creates an empty /app/re.json with no content and no viable plan for constructing regex-replacement pairs; from this point it attempts to fill the file incrementally via str_replace without ever developing a generative strategy for the core challenge.
t_commit_evidence: At step 22 the first str_replace ERROR ('Invalid new_str parameter: []. No replacement was performed') locks the agent into a repeated edit-tool failure loop from which it never escapes; no valid JSON content is ever written.
t_surface_evidence: Step 22 produces the first visible ERROR message: 'Invalid new_str parameter: [],. No replacement was performed. new_str and old_str must be different.'
trigger_explanation: The agent understands chess piece movement (demonstrated in step 21) but has no knowledge of how to encode board-state transformations as regex substitution patterns. It never discovers the oracle approach (large pre-computed JSON of all positions). Instead it attempts to write regex patterns ad hoc, which proves impossible for general chess move generation.
forewarning_evidence: In step 21 the agent says: 'implementing a complete chess move generator using only regex is going to be very complex' and 'implementing a complete chess move generator using only regex substitutions is not practical' — explicit self-doubt before the tool-failure commit point at step 22.
